intended_object: The Riemannian distance metric on a connected (preconnected) Riemannian manifold: d(x,y) is the infimum of lengths of C¹ paths from x to y. It is packaged as a `MetricSpace` structure whose topology is the manifold topology. Inferred from the docstring and from the Mathlib extended-distance construction it builds on.
explanation:
The definition takes Mathlib's `EMetricSpace.ofRiemannianMetric`, whose `edist` is `riemannianEDist I`, the infimum of the lengths of C¹ paths, and whose topology is defeq to the manifold topology. It turns this into a `MetricSpace` with `EMetricSpace.toMetricSpace`, using the library's lemma `riemannianEDist_ne_top`: on a preconnected manifold every distance is finite. That lemma is proved by showing that the set of points at finite distance from x is clopen.

`EMetricSpace.toMetricSpace` keeps `edist` and the uniform structure. So the resulting distance is `(riemannianEDist I x y).toReal`, the standard Riemannian distance, and the topology stays the manifold topology.

The hypotheses fit what the construction needs:
- `T3Space` is what Mathlib's extended version already uses to get the T0 property.
- `PreconnectedSpace` is exactly what makes all distances finite. Without it, two points in different components are at distance ∞, so no real-valued metric of this kind exists.

Mathlib has only the pseudo-emetric and emetric versions; it has no real-valued `MetricSpace.ofRiemannianMetric`. The definition is therefore the natural refinement of the Mathlib construction, at its natural generality.
